catalog_quote: Sutton 1978 p.234: "This description also would generally hold good, at the structural level, for Wik-Ngatharra; the greatest differences between it and Wik-Ngathana are in the forms of the pronoun paradigms, in phonological developments, and in lexicon, not in morphosyntactic structure." ... p.235: "Distinctions of quality and length are made among the nuclei of stressed syllables. The classification (fixed and weight-blind, initial primary stress, compound/kin-term+name exceptions as listed-set, word domain) rests on the fieldworker-of-record's grammar sketch (1978 dissertation appendix, the only grammar sketch Glottolog lists for the Wik-Ngathan/Wik-Ngatharr language) plus his own 2021 restatement that names Wik-Ngatharr explicitly ('the vowel with primary word stress' in the first syllable) and Hale's 2021 note on unstressed-vowel reduction in Wik-Ngatharr. sources.citation: Hale, Kenneth L. (1976). Wik reflections of Middle Paman phonology. In Languages of Cape York. AIAS. pp. 50-60.
sources.access_detail: open copy posted by the author (located 2026-09-25); a digital copy (available on request)
sources.note: Historical-comparative segmental phonology only: Part A (pp. 50-53) gives Paman > Wik reflexes for stops, nasals, liquids, glides and vowels (incl. loss of *V2 in Wik Munkn/Me?n/Ngatr, vowel fronting, length); Part B (pp. 53-60) is a cognate list of Middle Paman stems with Wik reflexes. The words stress, accent, pitch, tone and prominence do not occur anywhere in the 11 pages; no statement of the word-stress or tone system of any Wik language.
